investors discussion, this is a 2-way exchange. We will be happy to take your questions after 
this particular session. 
 
The company has done wonderfully well in last quarter. We have done a record sales in the 
history of this company in any quarter in the last so many years. That is INR 19,448 crores. So, 
I think we are now on a path to reach to INR 1 lakh crores per year of sales. This is what our 
aim is. The INR 19,448 crores, if we multiply by 4 quarters, which should be INR 80,000 crores, 
but our aim is to reach to INR 1 lakh crores as early as possible. 
 
The steel sales are up by 27% Y-o-Y. EBITDA is up by 34% Y-o-Y despite of very bad weather 
in Odisha, a lot of rains were there. The iron ore mines were full of water. We could manage a 
fairly good production. And we are now going to ramp up further. Our aim is to reach to about 
11-million-ton production in this financial year as targeted earlier. 
 
We have reached to a level of about 4.79 million tons in H1. And the next, that is H2, we are 
aiming for 6 million tons. So, this is net steel, the gross steel may be about 11 million tons. The 
company is doing very well in terms of availability of the raw material, whether it is coking coal 
or it is iron ore or availability of pellets through our internal resources or other consumables.

We have seen in last 3 months' time, very topsy-turvy situation, where we found that there was 
a shortage of natural gas in the country and there was a shortage of propane. And this was 
difficult time basically because of this Hormuz issue or the Iran and U.S. war. So fortunately, 
we are having the coal gasification plant. 
 
And we switched over to coal gas, that is, syngas for many of the reheating furnaces, galvanizing

profitability. And still, we are continuing. We are not using propane or natural gas. We are using 
our coal gas, that is, coal syngas or you can say the gas through coal gasification route.

We have 2 blast furnaces in Angul and 2 blast furnaces in Raigarh. So, all 4 blast furnaces, they 
are doing well now. The new blast furnace, which we installed last year, which has reached to a 
level of about 10,000 tons per day, which is in Angul. 
 
Hopefully, we will ramp it up in this particular month, say, today is 23rd, so I think in 7 days'

tons and then December 12,000 tons per day. Availability of iron ore from OMC and NMDC is 
seamless. There is no problem. 
 
The problems related to land slide from NMDC route to Angul route, those are over now. 
Railway is working. And the water from mines is already receded. So now the operations at 
OMC, all 8 mines, they are working very well. So, our own mine, Kasia mines that also is being 
ramped up, and we are sourcing material from our own mines also. 
 
We have 2 pellet plants in Barbil, both are running well. And the pellet plant in Angul is also 
running well. So by and large, I would say that the company is in a very, very solid state, and 
we'll be making a record production in the Q3, which will be ending on December 2026. 
 
Q4, we are further looking very positive, and we feel that we'll be surpassing the records what 
we are going to make in Q3. I think Q4 will be much better. As far as the market is concerned, 
the market is supporting very well, though the input costs have gone up, but we could recover 
the entire input costs, and we could make some positive impact in NSR while we compare on 
the input costs.

are aiming that we'll continue making such performance in other 2 quarters also, that is Q3 and 
Q4. 
The exports are also picking up. We are doing about 100,000 tons of export every month, mainly 
hot-rolled coils, plates and some quantity in rails and the structures. We are hopeful the 
honourable Commerce Minister, Mr. Piyush Goyal, is already in Germany.

Sandeep Modi: 
Good afternoon everyone, myself Sandeep. Let me take you through Jindal Steel's consolidated 
financial performance for the Q2FY27. We have delivered our highest ever quarterly gross 
revenue of INR 19,448 crores, up 44% Y-o-Y, while net revenue increased 43% Y-o-Y to record 
INR 16,704 crores. 
 
This was driven by the record Q2 sales volume, as Mr. Sharma said, of 2.38 million tons and 
higher average selling prices, supported by a higher share of flats and a lower proportion of TMT 
within the long products.

Domestic sales accounted for approximately 92% of total volume. Our adjusted EBITDA stood 
at INR 2,504 crores, up 34% Y-o-Y, while adjusted EBITDA per ton increased 5% Y-o-Y to 
INR 10,529 per ton. The sequential moderation in EBITDA was primarily due to higher raw 
material and operating costs, notwithstanding the positive impact of higher volume and 
improved sales mix. 
 
Coming to the cost part, coking coal was a key cost impact, and it was within the guidance what 
we have given in the last call for $12 to $15 per ton. Power and fuel, as well as freight expenses, 
especially ocean freight, also increased sequentially. This impact was partly offset by better 
ASP. 
 
Our consolidated profit after tax was INR 771 crores compared with INR 844 crores in the 
preceding quarter. Our balance sheet strengthened during the quarter. Our consolidated net debt 
declined by INR 1,141 crores from INR 15,927 crores at the end of June to INR 14,786 crores 
as at September end. 
 
Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved from 1.71x to 1.51x. Cash and cash equivalents stood at 
INR 7,237 crores, providing substantial liquidity as we execute our growth program. Capex 
during Q2FY27 was INR 1,228 crores and in the whole H1 was INR 3,187 crores. 
 
We remain continue to disciplined capital allocation with investment directed towards our steel 
and supporting infrastructure businesses and a focus on returns as the newly commissioned 
facilities ramp up. Our stated framework envisages annual growth capex of approximately INR 
7,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores, primarily funded through internal accruals, while seeking to 
maintain net debt to EBITDA below 1.5x through the cycle. 
 
For the second half, our priorities are clear: stabilize and ramp up the expanded facilities, 
improve product mix, cost competitiveness, working capital management and maintain balance 
sheet discipline. 
 
With that, we can open the floor for questions. Thank you.

Akhilesh: 
Sir, my second question is now on this slurry pipeline. So now since it has been commissioned, 
do we see any benefit of to accrue in the remaining of FY27 as well or the benefit will start to 
come in from FY28 onwards only? And also, will there be any additional cost associated with 
the ramp-up, which could come as a surprise? 
V.R. Sharma: 
No, there is no additional cost because this is a pumping station basically, grinding and pumping 
station. So, all the grinding machines are in place, the pumping stations in place. The water 
arrangement, etc., everything is in place. We are getting water from government. There is no 
problem. 
 
And this water, when we make slurry, we maintain slurry in a particular density that is specific 
gravity, 1.8 to 2 level and the water we recover at Angul. So, in a way, the water consumption 
in Angul that is reduced because this water, when it goes there in Angul, we filter it and we 
recycle it. We don't throw water outside because we have a zero liquid discharge policy. 
 
Then your next question is the cost impact. Yes, there will be benefit out of it because the iron 
ore, which is being transported through trucks mainly, that will now be shifted through slurry 
pipeline. So today, we are receiving more than 700 trucks per day full of iron ore. They come 
from Barbil, Keonjhar area and they come to Angul. 
 
So, of the 700 trucks, at least 500 trucks will be eliminated now. Only 200 trucks will come, 
which are geographically in the area, whether we take the iron ore to Barbil or we take the iron 
ore to Angul. So, the cost will be same. So, it is better to bring that iron ore to Angul in place of 
taking the iron ore to Barbil. 
 
So Barbil grinding station is in place and Barbil pumping house is in place. Now we have to run 
it on a daily basis. Hopefully, from day after tomorrow, this will continue non-stop till infinite

Amit Dixit: 
Congratulations for good performance. Sir, just wanted to get the update on captive coal mining.

Yes. So together in Raigarh and Angul, we have total coal mining capacity about 15 million 
tons. And Gare Palma in Raigarh is about 4 million tons, approximate number I'm giving you. 
And the other mines are in Utkal, that is near to the plant in Angul.

mines. There was some delay or you can say there was some stoppage because of very heavy 
rains. I think from 10th of October onwards, everything is going very well. 
 
So, we are aiming that we'll be reaching to a level of about 65% to 70% of the total requirement, 
we will be meeting all from our coal mines. And it also depends upon the cost. We are sometimes 
getting very good deals from Coal India and also Mahanadi Coalfields, and we try to avail that 
deal also. 
 
And sometimes we need washed coal for our coal gasification plant if our washery is not doing 
well or if we need more washed coal. So that also we buy from outside. But by and large, 
everything is going very well. There is no problem. 
 
We'll be meeting out our entire requirement in the next year from our own coal mines and also 
depends upon the costing. If the cost advantages are there to buy something from outside that 
we'll be blending and we'll be buying from outside.
